title: Putting Transformer Theories to the Test
abstract: arXiv:2610.32104v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Several formal theories have been developed to characterize the capabilities and limitations of the transformer architecture, each employing different abstractions that capture different features of the architecture. Due to the differences in their underlying assumptions and conceptual frameworks, these theories can disagree in their predictions about what tasks transformers find easy or hard. We map out seven theories of transformer capability (Star-free, $\mathsf{AC}^0$, $\mathsf{TC}^0$, C-RASP, MPC, BAPO, and Sensitivity) and translate their results into a common matrix of predictions across a suite of tasks covering different computational structures. We provide new theoretical results to complete this matrix. We then evaluate theoretical predictions through controlled experiments measuring in-distribution sample complexity, length generalization, and pretrained language model performance. tldr: 该论文将七种关于Transformer能力的理论预测统一到同一矩阵中，并通过受控实验验证，发现没有任何单一理论能完全解释Transformer在不同计算任务上的表现。
en_tdlr: This paper unifies the predictions of seven formal theories of transformer capability into a common matrix and validates them through controlled experiments, finding that no single theory fully explains transformer performance across different computational tasks.
